project.name: Impilo — Adult Medicine Domain (bedside clinical calculators and classifications)
project.description:
Pure Java 21 adult-medicine primitives shared by the clinical plane. Renal: the CKD-EPI 2021 race-free eGFR equation with KDIGO GFR categories, and Cockcroft-Gault creatinine clearance. Hepatic: MELD and Child-Pugh. Respiratory: CURB-65 with CRB-65 as a separately banded instrument. Thrombosis: the Wells scores for DVT and PE. Metabolic: albumin-corrected calcium, glucose-corrected sodium, and the anion gap with its albumin correction and delta ratio. Neurological: the Glasgow Coma Scale. Critical care: SOFA. Anthropometry: body surface area by DuBois and Mosteller. Alongside these, WHO/ISH-shaped cardiovascular risk banding, the NYHA functional classification, the Rockwood Clinical Frailty Scale, generic cognitive-screen proportion banding, oral morphine equivalence, and a composite treatment burden index.
Every calculator shares one refusal discipline: when an input is missing, out of physiological range, mutually inconsistent, or outside the instrument's validated population, the result carries a named RefusalReason and a clinician-readable explanation rather than a default, a sentinel or a null that reads as normal. A missing measurement is never scored as a healthy one.
The library owns arithmetic, never policy. It computes numbers and applies published classifications; it never decides what to do about them. Action thresholds, referral triggers, alerting and recommendations live in governed CKP content, so a ministry can change one without a code release.
No Spring, no I/O, no Jackson — every reference value is a compiled constant, so the same arithmetic runs inside a service, a batch job or an offline package and builds without a network or a container.
